| Tool | Description | |------|-------------| | `read` | Use `read` for static web; browser only if needed. Put line ranges in `path`, never a separate range/offset/limit parameter: - `{"path":"notes.txt:450-455"}` reads lines 450-455; `{"path":"notes.txt:-5"}` reads the last 5. - Include the selector on every ranged call; repeating a bare path does not advance through the file. Path suffixes: - :50 or :50- starts at line 50; :50-200 inclusive; :50+150 counts lines; :-60 last 60. - Commas join ranges (:5-16,960-973) or individual lines (:19,59). - A single non-raw range also shows 1 line before and 3 after (:50-80 shows 49-83). - Non-raw reads (comma lists too) may add the open/close line of a cut block; only :raw stays exact. - :raw verbatim without anchors/prefixes; combine :2-4:raw or :raw:2-4 for exactly those lines. - Beside :raw a bare number is that one line (:17:raw), :17-:raw runs on. Sources: - Bare code: declarations only; re-read ONLY footer-named omissions, NEVER guess `..`/`…`. - Selected file: `[foo.ts#1A2B]` snapshot+lines. Copy `[FILENAME#TAG]` for anchored edits; NEVER invent tag. - Directory: complete root; child listings cap at 12 (`… N more`), read child; page via :N-M/:-N. - URLs: reader text/markdown, :raw original HTML; bare host:port needs trailing slash. - PDF/documents: extracted text; notebooks: editable cells; images: decoded inline. - Also, with selectors in xd://read/sources (read it before first use): - SQLite, archives (ZIP, TAR, 7z, RAR and more), JSON/JSONL by jq filter, video, SVG as image, merge conflicts. | | `bash` | Persistent bash 5.3. cwd will reset after each turn, don't rely on cd; `pty` = interactive. Internal URIs work as paths for builtins/coreutils, redirects, globs. In-process builtins, ahead of PATH: ast-grep, awk, b2sum, base32, base64, basename, cat, chmod, cksum, cmp, combine, comm, cp, cut, date, dd, df, diff, dirname, du, env, errno, fd, find, fold, grep, head, hostname, id, ifne, isutf8, jq, ln, ls, lsof, md5, md5sum, mkdir, mktemp, mv, nl, nohup, nproc, od, paste, pgrep, pidwait, pkill, printenv, ps, readlink, realpath, rg, rm, rmdir, rsync, sd, sed, seq, sg, sha1sum, sha224sum, sha256sum, sha384sum, sha512sum, shasum, sleep, sort, sponge, stat, strings, tac, tail, tar, tee, timeout, top, touch, tr, truncate, ts, uname, uniq, uptime, wc, which, whoami, xargs, yes. `async` defers finite results but keeps the deadline (default 300s); `timeout: 0` for watchers and long jobs. Don't trunc output by habit, result will be summarized and saved as an artifact. Long-lived services: - unique name; ready requires name; no async/timeout; pty defaults true. - ready needs log regex or port (both if given); host defaults 127.0.0.1, ready.timeout 30s. Non-`pty` calls still running after 60s (or 1s before `timeout`, if sooner) usually move to background job `bg_N` and keep running to `timeout`. No backgrounding when the client terminal runs the command or the job cap is reached. The result arrives automatically as a follow-up message. NEVER poll. | | `edit` | Hashline patches existing files; new files: `write`. Each file: `[PATH#TAG]`, `TAG` required 4-hex snapshot from latest `read`/`search`. Numbers: original `LINE:TEXT`, never hunk-shifted. `PUT N.=M:` replace inclusive N–M with `+` body (`N.=N` for one line); `PUT N*:` replace block N. `PUT N:` insert before/after N (`<1` head, `>$` tail). `PUT >N*:` insert after block N at sibling depth; inside, use `PUT >M:` at closer. `CUT N.=M`/`CUT N*` delete and capture, optionally as `@name`. `PUT N @name` paste at gap (omit name for anonymous CUT); `PUT N.=M @name`/`PUT N* @name` paste over range/block (name REQUIRED). Register pastes have NO body; named registers persist across calls. `REM` delete file; `MV DEST` rename after prior edits (quote spaced paths). - `:` ops only: body rows `+TEXT` verbatim incl. indent; lone `+` blank. Literal `- item`/`+ item` → `+- item`/`++ item`. NEVER `-`/bare context. Body length independent of range; delete with CUT, not empty PUT. - Touch displayed changed lines only; `…`, `..`, collapsed `N-M:` and out-of-window lines UNSEEN. Re-read first. Tight ranges: split nonadjacent changes; NEVER include keepers or start/end mid-expression/block. Pure addition uses gap PUT. - `*` requires multi-line opener, NEVER closer/last/inner statement; use range/gap for one statement. Anchor first decorator/attribute/doc-comment to include it; standalone comments need explicit range. - Markdown heading blocks run through deeper headings until next same/higher; after section `PUT >N*:`, end body with blank line. - NEVER restyle unrelated code. After EVERY edit tag/numbers change: use edit response or fresh `read`; stale tag/surprise → STOP, re-read. ``` [greet.py#A1B2] PUT 1*: +@cache +def greet(name): + print(name) [PLAN.md#3C4D] PUT >2: +- task ``` Cross-file move: `CUT 1* @fn` in source, then `PUT <1 @fn` in destination section. | | `ask` | Ask the user to fill in one HTML form; blocks until they submit or cancel. Ask only for materially different tradeoffs the user must decide. Default: act using code/config/docs/history and conventions. Several viable choices: pick conservative/standard, proceed, state choice. - `html`: one
of plain semantic HTML, rendered natively in the user's terminal. - NEVER
